concerns.message: Finding 6 contradicts itself on where `rumor` sits relative to the new pending → `covered` rule. Sentence 1 has the player get an active journal rumor for a pending type by buying it mid-interval toward a new cache, which is a charged `rumor`. Sentence 2 says any paid request whose type is pending is `covered` and never charged. A type becomes pending only when a free trigger is capped, which requires every copy to be carried. After that, a purchase is essentially the only way the player can get a live journal rumor for that type. If pending → `covered` outranks `rumor`, the drop-at-boundary branch is almost unreachable. If it only replaces `capped` (the carrier-only case), sentence 1 works. decisions.md says `covered` is for 'a purchase the boundary would give for free', but the earlier rule says a pending type is dropped at the boundary once it is no longer carrier-only, so the boundary would not give it.
concerns.consequence: If the worker puts `covered` above `rumor`: once a cache appears, the player is told `covered` (and targetedRumorAvailability tells the UI not to buy), then gets nothing at the boundary because the pending type is dropped as no longer carrier-only. They lose a lead they wanted to pay for, which breaks §11's recovery intent. The 'pending drop' row in item 7's table also can't be built from a real scenario, so the coverage reviewer blocks again. Settle it as: pending → `covered` applies only when the request would otherwise be `capped` (still carrier-only). A request with a source or cache target is a charged `rumor`, and the pending entry is dropped at the next boundary.

concerns.message: Item 7 lets 'a failing check' stand in for a failing test. A careless deletion (removing a helper, leaving a variable unused under noUnusedLocals, or an unused import) fails typecheck, and the table would record that as proof of coverage. The typecheck exception is meant only for the reason narrowing, and the validator exception only for the alignment. The task also never says how big a 'branch' is. The pending set or `answerRequests` for each outcome could each be one deletion or several.
concerns.consequence: The table can look complete while some branches still have no behavioural test. The next coverage review finds one, and a fifth follow-up starts, which is exactly what this round is meant to prevent. Require every mutation except the narrowing to typecheck: flip the condition to a constant true or false, or make the function return early. Also give one table row per condition or outcome arm, each naming a vitest test ID.

concerns.message: Finding 5's 'only possible target is a carrier sighting' must be computed by the same eligibility function that rumor generation uses. That means sources before caches, excluding claimed-out islands, the player's own inventory, and duel-reserved copies. If `answerRequests` and `targetedRumorAvailability` each re-derive it, they can disagree on edge cases. Two examples: a copy that is reserved in a duel, and a type whose carriers are missing from the newer snapshot because the copy was picked up after the last boundary. In both, `covered` promises broadcast information that doesn't contain the type.
concerns.consequence: The UI shows 'covered' while the step answers `rumor` (or the reverse), so the player is charged unexpectedly or told not to buy something that isn't free. The agreement test passes only on the chosen fixtures. Share one predicate between the step and `targetedRumorAvailability`, and add a fixture where the type is absent from the newer snapshot.

concerns.message: Finding 6 says 'added earlier in this same step'. The fixes-3 design gathers triggers into a set keyed by (player, type), so a step has no order. A worker who implements 'earlier' literally, for example by checking pending during a sequential pass, brings back the order dependence that fixes-3 removed by construction.
concerns.consequence: The all-orders phase tests or the permutation property run catch it late, or worse, a purchase listed before the capped free trigger is charged `capped` or `sighting` in one order and `covered` in another. The rule should be 'pending after gather', whatever the arrival order.

concerns.message: Existing tests and property-checker expectations after minute 28 probably assume that a paid carrier-only request is a charged `sighting`, for example the `EXERCISED` coverage or the real-constants 36,000-tick seed. Finding 5 changes those expectations, and the task allows that only if the report names each one. Running the long seed once per mutation across about 15 branches also eats into the 75-minute budget.
concerns.consequence: The worker either changes property assertions quietly, which reviewers flag, or runs out of time on the mutation table. Run the mutations against the intel test files only, with the short seeds, and list every changed post-28 expectation in the report.

structured_output.simpler_alternative: Handle findings 5 and 6 with one pure predicate, `freeCoverage(state, view, player, type)`, used by both `answerRequests` and `targetedRumorAvailability`. It returns `covered` when (a) the reveal has happened and the type's only eligible target is a carrier, or (b) the type is pending after gather and still carrier-only. In every other case the request is decided as before (`rumor` if there is a source or cache target, and the pending entry is dropped at the next boundary because it is no longer sighting-eligible or the player has a live rumor). One predicate means one table row per clause, the step and the UI can't disagree, and the drop branch is reachable through an ordinary purchase. For item 7, list every mutation as a one-line diff that still typechecks (condition → constant) in `docs/intel.md` with the vitest test ID it kills, so a reviewer can re-apply each one.
structured_output.cheap_experiment: Before changing anything, write one scripted test on the restored snapshot. In it, player P has a capped free trigger (every copy of Moon carried) so Moon is pending. In a later non-boundary step, a cache holding a Moon copy appears (an expired reservation) and P buys Moon. Record what the snapshot answers and what the next boundary delivers to P. If the boundary drops Moon because it is no longer carrier-only, then answering that purchase `covered` leaves P with nothing. That shows `covered` must replace only `capped`, not `rumor`, and settles finding 6's precedence before the worker builds on it.
